purpose: Provider-neutral translation aid data for BridgeTranslate implementations.

aids.plain_label: I describe things by what they do or how I know them
aids.example: I may remember the role, story, location or function before the formal name.
aids.bridge_action: Match the description to supplied context or evidence, propose a supported label, and never invent a proper name.

aids.plain_label: My thoughts arrive as a connected map
aids.example: Several linked details may arrive before the central point becomes visible.
aids.bridge_action: Capture all nodes and relationships before creating chronology or categories.

aids.plain_label: My information comes out in a different order
aids.example: Please organise it without deleting context that arrived early or late.
aids.bridge_action: Sequence the account after mapping and show the result back to the user.

aids.plain_label: I can understand or do it but cannot name the formal rule
aids.example: I may use language or systems accurately without knowing the textbook term.
aids.bridge_action: Supply optional external labels without testing or downgrading the user's competence.

aids.plain_label: I understand the words but not what the form is really asking
aids.example: Explain the function of the question before asking me to answer it.
aids.bridge_action: State the hidden format, evidence or outcome the question requests in concrete language.

aids.plain_label: Abstract ideas need a map, example or practical anchor
aids.example: I understand better when the idea has a structure, example or observable effect.
aids.bridge_action: Translate abstraction into examples, flows, maps or practical prompts.

aids.example: A word, date, connection or feeling may become available after I begin answering.
aids.bridge_action: Allow additions and corrections without treating them as automatic inconsistency.

aids.example: I may know the information but lose access to it during conflict, urgency or questioning.
aids.bridge_action: Use written recognition prompts, allow pauses, and mark uncertain recall rather than forcing certainty.

aids.plain_label: Dates and sequence are hard to retrieve
aids.example: I may remember the event and relationships more clearly than the exact date.
aids.bridge_action: Use documents to anchor dates and otherwise label the date as approximate or unclear.

aids.plain_label: Feelings are hard to identify or name
aids.example: I may recognise impact or urgency before I can label the emotion.
aids.bridge_action: Accept observable impact and do not force or invent an emotional label.

aids.plain_label: Body signals are hard to identify or explain
aids.example: I may notice a change in function before I can describe the sensation.
aids.bridge_action: Separate observed function, possible sensation and confirmed interpretation.

aids.plain_label: Stress changes how well I can communicate
aids.example: I may lose words, speech, memory or sequencing when overloaded.
aids.bridge_action: Keep the route written, pause-friendly and low-density.

aids.plain_label: Sensory load reduces my communication capacity
aids.example: Noise, light, movement, pain or crowded information may reduce access to words and decisions.
aids.bridge_action: Reduce density and decisions and preserve information about the conditions affecting access.

aids.plain_label: My tone, accent or wording changes with the person or setting
aids.example: The style may change while the underlying meaning remains stable.
aids.bridge_action: Do not treat register variation as deception; translate for the intended audience while preserving meaning.

aids.plain_label: I communicate only or most reliably in writing
aids.example: Do not require a voice response or telephone conversation.
aids.bridge_action: Keep every instruction, question, consent and correction available in writing.

aids.plain_label: I use AAC, selected options or another person to support communication
aids.example: Typed, symbol-based, selected or supported input is my communication.
aids.bridge_action: Address the user directly and accept the chosen communication method as valid.

aids.example: Use short sections, clear spacing and concrete language.
aids.bridge_action: Reduce text density without deleting necessary meaning.

aids.plain_label: English is not my first or strongest language
aids.bracket_label: multilingual / English as an additional language
aids.example: Avoid unnecessary idioms and ask before replacing culturally specific meaning.
aids.bridge_action: Use clear language and label translation uncertainty separately from event uncertainty.

aids.plain_label: I am not sure which description fits
aids.example: Help me recognise useful support without requiring a label.
aids.bridge_action: Offer concrete examples and let the user select what helps.
